# StepCheck Dev

> Deterministic context firewall for AI coding agents: AST-skeleton checkouts, three commit gates (A mechanical, B omission, C executed invariants) and DSSE attestations, served as a Streamable HTTP MCP server and a BYOK proxy. 50-turn benchmark: 120,815 raw tokens -> 15,039 sent (87.6% saved), 4/4 injected faults caught.

Apache-2.0. Python projects for now. This file is generated by `stepcheck llms` from the repository's own files.

## Kernel seams

- [StateKernel (Seam 1)](https://github.com/lalithasutam/stepcheck-dev/blob/main/backend/kernel/__init__.py): init_session, checkout(focus=), commit(patch=) through Gates A/B/C, lock_node, provenance (in-toto Statement v1)
- [DualDoorGateway (Seam 2)](https://github.com/lalithasutam/stepcheck-dev/blob/main/backend/server.py): Door 1 BYOK firewall proxy for /v1/messages and /v1/chat/completions; Door 2 REST /v1/step/* plus MCP at /mcp
- [CLI](https://github.com/lalithasutam/stepcheck-dev/blob/main/backend/cli.py): stepcheck up / benchmark / review / preview / audit / ci / llms
- [Agent rules](https://github.com/lalithasutam/stepcheck-dev/blob/main/CLAUDE.md): the MCP workflow Claude Code and Cursor follow: session, focused checkout, patch commit, omission check

## Benchmarks

- [benchmarks/results.json](https://github.com/lalithasutam/stepcheck-dev/blob/main/benchmarks/results.json): the 50-turn coding-rot benchmark receipt every figure above is read from
- [Interactive 50-turn replay](https://lalithasutam.github.io/stepcheck-dev/): turn scrubber, OKF graph, patch diff, attestation and cost curve; no install
- [Audit receipt](https://lalithasutam.github.io/stepcheck-dev/audit.html): anonymized stepcheck audit of real Claude Code sessions: cache-cliff re-writes and Read-tool bloat
- [CI](https://github.com/lalithasutam/stepcheck-dev/actions/workflows/ci.yml): pytest at the two public seams plus stepcheck ci on Ubuntu and Windows

## Quickstart

- [README](https://github.com/lalithasutam/stepcheck-dev#run-turnkey): pipx install git+https://github.com/lalithasutam/stepcheck-dev, then stepcheck audit and stepcheck up
- [MCP for Claude Code](https://github.com/lalithasutam/stepcheck-dev#claude-code-slash-commands-work-out-of-the-box-after-cloning): claude mcp add --transport http stepcheck http://127.0.0.1:8420/mcp/ and the four shipped slash commands
- [Release v0.3.2](https://github.com/lalithasutam/stepcheck-dev/releases/tag/v0.3.2): source and the self-contained studio preview

## Optional

- [GLOSSARY](https://github.com/lalithasutam/stepcheck-dev/blob/main/GLOSSARY.md): ubiquitous language: OKF frame, gates, seams, attestation

# README.md

# StepCheck Dev

[![CI](https://github.com/lalithasutam/stepcheck-dev/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/lalithasutam/stepcheck-dev/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
**Live:** [131-session audit receipt](https://lalithasutam.github.io/stepcheck-dev/audit.html) · [50-turn interactive replay](https://lalithasutam.github.io/stepcheck-dev/)

**Cloudflare + pre-commit for coding agents.** A deterministic layer between your agent and the model that
stops two things that go wrong in every long session: the agent quietly drops a decorator or a guard clause
around turn 25 because the file it is editing has been sitting in context as a stale 500-line read, and you
pay for all of those reads again at full price every time you pause longer than the provider's cache window.
Teams get the same problem multiplied: more AI pull requests than a senior engineer can review for cross-file
omissions, on a frontier-model bill driven by trivial edits over uncompacted history.

**Three steps, none of them in your prompt:**

1. `stepcheck audit --card` — sixty seconds, no server: reads your local Claude Code transcripts and shows the
   dollars lost to cache-cliff re-reads, the share of Read tokens spent on bodies the agent never used, and
   the exact turns where a decorator or guard went missing. Nothing but totals leaves the machine.
2. `stepcheck hooks && stepcheck up` — invisible daily protection: a `PreToolUse` hook turns large file reads
   into AST skeletons, every edit runs Gates A/B/C (dropped decorator or guard: blocked; changed signature:
   callers flagged `DIRTY_OMISSION_RISK`), and the `Stop` hook refuses to end the turn until those callers are
   re-verified.
3. Door 1 proxy + PR bot — for teams: accordion compaction of old tool results, a cache-cliff shield, gate-backed
   routing of focused edits to a cheaper model, and `stepcheck ci --report` (or the GitHub Action) posting a
   blast-radius and in-toto provenance checklist on every PR.

| Tier | Who | What it unlocks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Open core (free, Apache-2.0) | every developer | audit card, hooks, the gateway, Gates A/B/C, MCP, Studio |
| Pro FinOps proxy ($19/mo or 15% of verified savings) | heavy API / BYOK users | all-turn accordion compaction, cache-cliff shield, `x-stepcheck-tier: auto` arbitrage |
| Team PR & FinOps ($39/seat/mo) | 10–100 seat teams | GitHub Action PR bot, `GET /v1/team/summary` ledger, org-wide Pin & Lock |
| Enterprise Trust Ledger ($79/seat/mo or self-hosted) | regulated engineering orgs | polyglot monorepo verification, `stepcheck compliance` DUC / DUA-E bundles |

Licensing is opt-in (`STEPCHECK_REQUIRE_KEY=1`); with it unset everything in this repository runs locally with no
key. Ubiquitous language and the two public testing seams live in `GLOSSARY.md`.

## Layout

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `backend/kernel/` | **StateKernel** (Seam 1): OKF graph compilation, bounded `checkout(focus=)` with AST skeleton slicing, 3-tier gated `commit(source= \| patch=)` with diff folding (A mechanical/locked · B omission · C semantic invariants over `src`/`tree`/`ns`, auto-mined from leading `if …: raise` guards with zero annotations), DSSE/SHA-256 attestation, draft GC, cache-cliff telemetry |
| `backend/server.py` | **DualDoorGateway** (Seam 2): Door 1 firewall proxy (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages`, BYOK or dry-run) with three-band accordion compaction and opt-in tier routing, Door 2 REST `/v1/step/*` (incl. the warm `POST /v1/step/hook` lifecycle-hook evaluator) + FastMCP Streamable HTTP at `/mcp` + `WS /v1/ws/{session_id}` |
| `backend/tests/` | 272 tests, all at the two seams, zero mocks of internals (incl. the 50-turn ≥85% benchmark gate, self-hosted compaction floors, latency budgets, a 10-class fault-injection matrix, the wild-corpus hardening cases, dotted method slicing, multi-definition symbol groups, budget laundering and in-toto provenance) |
| `frontend/` | StepCheck Studio: React + TS + Vite + Tailwind, @xyflow/react OKF graph (Pin & Lock), Monaco DiffEditor + attestation viewer, live gate feed + cost chart, WS-driven; replays a built-in demo session when no gateway is reachable |
| `extension/` | VS Code / Cursor webview wrapper (`StepCheck: Open Studio`) |
| `benchmarks/` | 50-turn coding-rot benchmark (events injected at T20/T25/T35/T36; 87.6% tokens saved) + review generator |
| `architecture-review.html` | Generated visual report |
| `stepcheck-studio-preview.html` | Zero-dependency interactive replay of the 50-turn run (turn scrubber, graph, patch diff, attestation, cost curve) |
| `backend/cli.py` + `pyproject.toml` | `stepcheck up / benchmark / review / preview / audit [--card] / ci [--report] / llms / hooks` — `hooks [path]` installs idempotent Claude Code hook wiring under `.claude/` that calls the gateway's `/v1/step/hook` and allows when the daemon is offline; `ci --report` writes the PR blast-radius and provenance checklist; `audit --card` writes an anonymized SVG badge; `llms` regenerates `docs/llms.txt` + `docs/llms-full.txt` (llmstxt.org) from the repo's own files, so AI search engines quote the measured figures; `ci [path]` is the headless PR gatekeeper: every module must parse, match its DSSE attestation, hold no `DIRTY_OMISSION_RISK`, and pass Gates A/B/C with all invariants executed (exit 1 names the module and violation); `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs it on Ubuntu + Windows |
| `backend/audit.py` | `stepcheck audit [path]`: reads Claude Code `~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl`, receipts cache-cliff waste vs skeleton checkouts and dropped-decorator/guard edits + their retry loops → `stepcheck-audit.html` (falls back to `benchmarks/fixtures/sample_session.jsonl`) |
| `CLAUDE.md` → `.cursorrules` | Agent rules: enforces the StepCheck MCP workflow (init → focused checkout → patch commit → omission check + savings) in Claude Code and Cursor |

## Run (turnkey)

```bash
pipx install git+https://github.com/lalithasutam/stepcheck-dev   # the `stepcheck` CLI, no clone needed
pip install -e .            # …or from a clone (editable)
(cd frontend && npm install && npm run build)   # once: compiled Studio served at /studio
stepcheck up                # one port (:8420): Studio UI + Door 1 proxy + REST + MCP + WS
stepcheck benchmark         # 50-turn coding-rot benchmark
stepcheck review            # architecture-review.html
stepcheck preview           # stepcheck-studio-preview.html (self-contained replay)
stepcheck audit             # your own cache-cliff waste + Read-tool bloat, no server needed → stepcheck-audit.html
stepcheck ci backend        # headless gate: parse + attestations + Gates A/B/C for every module (CI/PR)
stepcheck llms              # docs/llms.txt + docs/llms-full.txt from README, GLOSSARY, LAUNCH and benchmarks/results.json
stepcheck hooks             # .claude/hooks + settings wiring: Read over threshold -> skeleton, Edit of a locked module -> deny, Stop while dirty -> block
stepcheck ci . --report     # the headless gate plus a Markdown PR checklist: touched modules, re-verified callers, conserved symbols, in-toto digests
stepcheck audit --card      # stepcheck-audit-card.svg + a copy-paste badge line; file names and session ids never appear
```

## Door 1: accordion compaction and tier routing

Every proxied turn through `/v1/messages` or `/v1/chat/completions` passes a three-band compactor: the last
four messages stay verbatim, older Python source blocks over 150 tokens are replaced in place by their AST
skeleton, dead-end turns are pruned, and after a cache-cliff gap the oldest band folds into one OKF
session-state frame. The dry-run response carries a `stepcheck.compaction` block with per-band token counts.
Routing is opt-in: `x-stepcheck-tier: auto` (or `STEPCHECK_TIER_POLICY=auto`) sends a focused single-symbol
turn to `STEPCHECK_FAST_MODEL` first and re-sends it to the requested frontier model only when a gate rejects
the draft; without the header nothing changes.

## TypeScript and JavaScript projects

`.ts`, `.tsx`, `.js` and `.jsx` files are indexed next to `.py` (declaration files, `node_modules`, `dist`,
`build` and `out` are skipped). Relative imports become graph edges, top-level declarations render as
brace-elided skeletons, patch ops splice exact line spans, and Gates A/B plus the DSSE attestation apply
unchanged; Gate C has no invariants for TypeScript yet, and class members are not individually addressable.

Checkouts and patch ops address methods too: `focus=["StateKernel.commit"]` emits that one method verbatim inside a
class skeleton, and `replace_symbol` / `delete_symbol` on `"Class.method"` splice only its lines. A name always
addresses its whole definition group (`@overload` stubs + implementation, a `@property` with its setter).
`StateKernel.provenance(session_id, node_id)` exports the latest attestation as an in-toto Statement v1 inside a
DSSE envelope (`application/vnd.in-toto+json`), the shape cosign and Witness consume; the signature is the kernel's
deterministic SHA-256 scheme, not a key.

## Claude Code slash commands (work out of the box after cloning)

`.claude/commands/` ships four project commands. They need the gateway running (`stepcheck up`) and the
`stepcheck` MCP server connected (`claude mcp add --transport http stepcheck http://127.0.0.1:8420/mcp/`);
`CLAUDE.md` supplies the rules they enforce.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/stepcheck-session [node_id …]` | Brings `:8420` up if needed, calls `init_project_session` on the repo root, locks the named modules (`lock_module_invariants`), prints the live Studio URL `…/studio/?session=<id>` |
| `/stepcheck-fix <issue>` | Fixes the issue strictly through the gates: Red→Green test at a public seam, `checkout_context_frame` with a narrow `focus`, surgical `commit_verified_step` patch, re-verifies every `DIRTY_OMISSION_RISK` dependent until `can_finalize: true`, reports attestation sha256s and token savings |
| `/stepcheck-ci [message]` | Runs `stepcheck ci .` (zero dirty nodes, zero SHA-256 drift, Gates A/B/C on every module) and the full `pytest -q`; only then commits with the given message (push only when asked) |
| `/stepcheck-audit [path] [--limit N]` | Runs `stepcheck audit` on local Claude Code transcripts and summarises cache-cliff waste, Read-tool bloat vs AST skeletons, and the regressions a gate would have blocked |

## Run (development)

```bash
# backend + tests
cd backend && pip install -r requirements.txt && python -m pytest -q
python server.py                         # gateway on :8420 (PORT overrides)

# frontend
cd frontend && npm install && npm run dev   # Studio on :5173
# open http://localhost:5173/?session=<session_id from POST /v1/step/init>

# benchmark + report
python3 benchmarks/coding_rot_benchmark.py
python3 benchmarks/generate_review.py

# extension (compile check; load the folder via VS Code "Run Extension")
cd extension && npm install && npm run compile
```

## Door 1 in one call

```bash
SID=$(curl -s localhost:8420/v1/step/init -d '{"project_root":"/path/to/project"}' \
      -H 'content-type: application/json' | jq -r .session_id)
curl -s localhost:8420/v1/messages \
  -H "x-stepcheck-session: $SID" -H "x-stepcheck-node: billing" \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"claude-sonnet-4-5","max_tokens":512,"messages":[...]}'
# add x-api-key + x-stepcheck-upstream (or STEPCHECK_UPSTREAM_BASE) to forward BYOK;
# without them you get the deterministic dry-run with stepcheck.sent_messages.
```

## Testing rules (skill precedence)

`tdd` + `codebase-design` override `python-testing-patterns` on mocking: never
mock internal modules, AST parsers, YAML validators, or hash functions. Tests
hit Seam 1 / Seam 2 only, against concrete non-tautological fixtures
(hand-written projects, hand-calculated telemetry numbers).

## Security model

Gate C exec-loads the agent's staged module in an isolated namespace under a step/time guard so
callable invariants can run against it. That is an isolated namespace, **not a security sandbox**:
run the gateway in a container when the agent is untrusted. Python projects only for now.

## License

Apache-2.0 — see `LICENSE` and `NOTICE`. Everything in this repository is the open core (kernel,
gates, MCP server, BYOK proxy, Studio, `stepcheck ci` and `stepcheck audit`). If StepCheck gets real
use, the paid product will be a team layer (shared attestation ledger, org-wide CI gate); the core
stays open.

# Launch write-up

(order: the problem → your own bill → how it works → the benchmark with its caveat → try it → limits → the ask → license):

I kept watching long agent sessions go bad the same way. Around turn 30 the model quietly deletes a decorator it stopped reading, the tests it still runs pass, and the bill is climbing because every turn re-reads every file. If you're past Anthropic's 5-minute cache window between turns (real refactors are), you pay full input rate for all of it again.

I measured the bill half on my own logs. `stepcheck audit` reads the Claude Code transcripts under `~/.claude/projects`: across 131 sessions and 7,612 assistant turns, 95 turns resumed after the cache had expired and re-wrote 5.88M tokens of context at full rate — $15.87 above cache-read price — and 1.6M tokens were pulled with the Read tool where the same files as AST skeletons would have been 0.4M. The anonymized receipt is linked below.

StepCheck is a small deterministic layer between the agent and the model that fixes both halves.

Context: the repo gets compiled into an OKF graph, one Markdown frame per module with strict YAML frontmatter (exports, deps, preserved symbols, invariants, attestations). The agent checks out one node at a time. With `focus=[charge]` it gets that function verbatim and the rest of the module as an AST skeleton: signatures, decorators, docstrings, bodies replaced with `...`, runs of constants folded to one line. Dependencies come as interface skeletons only. The agent commits a patch of AST ops (append / replace_symbol / delete_symbol) and the kernel folds it into canonical state. Telemetry charges the patch, not the module.

Correctness: every commit runs three gates before it lands.
- Gate A, mechanical: parses, exported names dependents import still exist, locked modules refuse everything.
- Gate B, omission: AST symbol fingerprinting. Drop a `@audit` decorator the frame lists in `preserved_symbols[]` and you get `OmissionError(INTRA_NODE_SYMBOL_DROPPED)`. Change an exported signature and the dependents flip to `DIRTY_OMISSION_RISK`; the session can't finalize until each one is checked out and re-verified.
- Gate C, logical: invariants in the frame's frontmatter, evaluated against `src` (normalized via `ast.unparse`, so whitespace can't trip them and comments can't satisfy them), `tree`, and `ns`, the staged module exec-loaded in an isolated namespace with project imports resolved to canonical sources. `call:charge("acct", 0) raises ValueError` is a one-liner, and you usually don't write it: leading `if …: raise` guards are mined into invariants automatically at index time. Runs under a step/wall-clock guard so a runaway loop is a deterministic LogicalError, not a hung process.

A passing commit appends a DSSE-style SHA-256 envelope to the frame. Replay the same session on another machine and you get byte-identical envelopes.

Two doors: a BYOK proxy for `/v1/chat/completions` and `/v1/messages` that prunes dead-end turns and injects the compact frame, and a Streamable HTTP MCP server at `/mcp` for Claude Code / Cursor. One port, `stepcheck up`.

Numbers: my synthetic 50-turn benchmark on a 6-module repo sends 15,039 tokens where the raw agent sends 120,815 (87.6% less), and it catches all four injected faults — T20 silent `@audit` drop, T25 signature change dirtying two dependents and blocking finalize, T35 guard removed with identical statement count, T36 mutation of a locked module. It's my benchmark, so read it as a ceiling, not a promise: `stepcheck benchmark` reproduces it and the replay below lets you scrub every turn. 272 tests at the two public seams, zero mocks of internals, CI green on Ubuntu and Windows.

Try it in 60 seconds (the audit needs no server and prints your own number):

    pipx install git+https://github.com/lalithasutam/stepcheck-dev
    stepcheck audit        # your cache-cliff waste + Read-tool bloat from ~/.claude/projects
    stepcheck up           # then: claude mcp add --transport http stepcheck http://127.0.0.1:8420/mcp/

Honest limits: Gate C exec-loads the agent's staged module in an isolated namespace under a step/time guard — that is not a security sandbox, so run the gateway in a container for untrusted agents. Python projects only for now. And the benchmark is mine.

What I'd like feedback on: the invariant ladder (string over normalized `src` → AST → callable `call:` form — is that the right shape?), and your own `stepcheck audit` numbers: sessions, turns, dollars above cache-read, Read-tool tokens vs skeletons. There's a pinned Discussion for receipts; please don't post raw transcripts, they contain your code.

Apache-2.0. If this gets real use, the paid thing will be a team layer (shared attestation ledger, org-wide CI gate); the core stays open.

- Repo: https://github.com/lalithasutam/stepcheck-dev
- 50-turn interactive replay: https://lalithasutam.github.io/stepcheck-dev/ (jump to a moment: [T20](https://lalithasutam.github.io/stepcheck-dev/#t20), [T25](https://lalithasutam.github.io/stepcheck-dev/#t25), [T35](https://lalithasutam.github.io/stepcheck-dev/#t35), [T36](https://lalithasutam.github.io/stepcheck-dev/#t36))
- 131-session anonymized audit receipt: https://lalithasutam.github.io/stepcheck-dev/audit.html

# GLOSSARY.md

# StepCheck Dev — GLOSSARY

Ubiquitous language for the Anti-Context-Rot State Engine. Use these terms exactly, in code,
tests, frames, and UI. Scope: AI coders, engineering teams, multi-agent swarms (Segments 1–3).

## Core nouns

**OKFFrame** — One Markdown document with *strict* YAML frontmatter that is the canonical,
compacted representation of one code module (one Python file). Frontmatter keys:
`node_id`, `path`, `status`, `exports[]` (name + signature), `deps[]` (node_ids),
`preserved_symbols[]`, `invariants[]` (executable Python assertions over `src`),
`verified[]` (append-only DSSE attestation envelopes), `locked` (bool).
Body: a short generated summary + the current source fenced block. Frontmatter that fails
strict parsing (missing keys, wrong types, duplicate keys) is a `MechanicalError` at index time.

**OKF graph** — The project-level artifact: `index.md` (project frame listing every node and
edge) plus one OKFFrame per module, linked by `deps[]`. It is a DAG over `node_id`s; an import
cycle collapses into mutual dep edges (no dirty-propagation infinite loops: propagation visits
each node once).

**node_id** — A module's file stem while that stem is unique in the project (`billing`); when
stems collide (several `__init__.py`, `pkg/models.py` + `other/models.py`) the colliding files use
their dotted relative path (`kernel.__init__`, `other.models`). `deps[]` are resolved through
packages: absolute and relative imports (`from . import _gates`, `from kernel import StateKernel`)
both land on the right node — at any nesting depth: a **lazy import** inside a function, an
`if TYPE_CHECKING:` block or a `try: … except ImportError:` fallback is a dependency too — and Gate A checks the names a dependent imports against the staged
module's top-level bindings. Gate C loads a package module as a package, so its relative imports
resolve to canonical sources. **Source roots:** a session rooted at the repository also resolves
names relative to a first-level directory that code puts on `sys.path` (`src/`, `backend/`): with
the root at the repo, `from kernel import StateKernel` in `backend/server.py` still resolves to
`backend/kernel/__init__.py`, and the Gate C sandbox binds that alias to the canonical source. An
alias only resolves while it is unambiguous, never when its top-level name is a standard-library
module (`utils/json.py` does not capture `import json`); a root-relative name always wins over an alias.

**Session persistence** — Every session is written to `<root>/.stepcheck/sessions/<session_id>.json`
on each state change and indexed in `~/.stepcheck/sessions.json` (`STEPCHECK_HOME` overrides the
directory). A fresh `StateKernel` (a gateway restart) rehydrates a known `session_id` on first use;
an unknown or malformed id is a `KeyError` (404 at Seam 2). `StateKernel(ephemeral=True)` is
verification-only: gates, attestations and the graph work in memory, but no frame, session file,
registry entry or tracked-file write-back is ever written — this is what `stepcheck ci` runs on.
**Session refresh:** `refresh_sessions()` reconciles memory with disk — a session whose file was
archived or deleted is evicted (its next use is the `KeyError` of an unknown id), and one whose file
another process rewrote (newer `mtime_ns`, bytes not this process's own last write) is reloaded.
The gateway runs it before every `/v1/…` and `/mcp` request, so a long-lived daemon never answers
the Stop hook from a session already archived on disk.

**StateKernel** — The single deep module behind Seam 1. Owns OKF compilation, sessions,
checkout/commit, the three gates, locking, attestation, and telemetry. Everything else in
`backend/kernel/` is private implementation (`_`-prefixed modules), not interface.

**CheckoutPayload** — What `checkout()` returns: the target OKFFrame (full, or sliced by
`focus`), its immediate verified dependencies as **interface skeletons**, the locked
invariants that constrain the edit, and `token_count`. Hard budget: `token_count < 4000`.
Never contains unrelated sibling frames. An unfocused checkout whose frame would meet the
budget auto-falls back to a pure skeleton + symbol index (`auto_skeletonized=True`). Superseded attestations fold into one
`attestation: {count, latest_sha256, latest_turn}` summary in the payload; the on-disk frame
keeps the append-only `verified[]` chain. **Compact header:** when a focused checkout's cone
covers every top-level symbol (the frame is the whole module, served verbatim) or the full header
would outweigh the file, the frontmatter shrinks to `node_id, path, status, locked` (+ `deps`,
`attestation` when non-empty); everything dropped is still enforced at the gates. Empty
dependency / invariant sections are omitted from the payload. **Pragma bypass (zero inflation):**
when the focus covers every symbol of the module and even the compact frame would cost more
tokens than the raw source, the payload is one comment line — `# [stepcheck: <node_id> | <status>
| invariants: N enforced]` (`//` outside Python) — followed by the source verbatim; `rendered()`
returns exactly that. The overhead is that one line, never a frame.

**Focus / AST skeleton** — `checkout(…, focus=[names])` serves the named top-level defs
verbatim (comments included) and every other def/class as decorators + signature + docstring +
`...`, with runs of module-level assignments folded into one summary line. `focus=[]` is a pure
skeleton; `focus=None` is the full frame.

**Patch (diff folding)** — `commit(…, patch=[ops])` folds AST-level ops into the node's canonical
state before the gates run: `{"op":"append","code"}`, `{"op":"replace_symbol","name","code"}`
(decorators included), `{"op":"delete_symbol","name"}`. Telemetry charges the patch, not the
module. A patch that cannot fold is a `MechanicalError` at Gate A.

**CommitVerdict** — What `commit()` returns: `accepted: bool`, `gate` (`"A" | "B" | "C" | None`),
`error` (a `GateError` or `None`), `attestation` (envelope dict when accepted), `dirtied[]`
(node_ids transitioned to `DIRTY_OMISSION_RISK`), `reverified[]` (dependents re-checked in memory
and re-attested instead — see OmissionRisk).

**PreservedSymbol** — A named AST element (decorator usage, guard clause marker, internal call,
exported def) listed in a frame's `preserved_symbols[]`. Silently dropping one is an
`OmissionError(subtype="INTRA_NODE_SYMBOL_DROPPED")` unless the commit passes
`allow_deletion=True`.

**OmissionRisk** — Node status `DIRTY_OMISSION_RISK`: a dependency's exported signature changed,
so this node may silently rely on stale behavior. A session cannot finalize while any node holds
this status; it clears only by checking the node out and re-committing it through all gates.
**In-kernel re-verification:** for a Python dependency, a dependent whose *contract* is intact —
no signature changed or removed among the names it imports (`from m import a`), or among the
public exports for a module import (`import m`) — is not dirtied: if it is clean and its on-disk
bytes still hash to what the session last attested, Gates A/B/C run on it in memory against the
new state and, on a pass, its attestation is refreshed (`CommitVerdict.reverified[]`). Purely
additive changes therefore dirty nothing. TS / Go / Rust / Java use the same per-name contract,
read from the export signatures (`Class.member` counts as `Class`; Go names are the identifiers
read off the package alias, `ledger.Open`); an export whose name cannot be parsed (`default`)
breaks every importer. A locked dependent that is dirtied clears by re-committing its locked bytes
unchanged (see Gate A).

**TokenFirewall** — Door 1 of the gateway: the BYOK proxy that intercepts bloated `messages[]`,
commits verified steps into the StateKernel, prunes dead-end exploration history, injects the
compact CheckoutPayload, and forwards upstream with the caller's own key (deterministic local
dry-run when no key is supplied).

**DualDoorGateway** — The whole HTTP surface (Seam 2): Door 1 (TokenFirewall proxy routes) +
Door 2 (explicit REST + Streamable HTTP MCP at `/mcp` + `WS /v1/ws/{session_id}`).

## Statuses

`ACTIVE` → editable; `VERIFIED` → last commit passed all gates (attested); `LOCKED` → verified
and pinned, any mutation rejected at Gate A; `DIRTY_OMISSION_RISK` → see OmissionRisk;
`REJECTED` → last commit failed a gate (frame content unchanged).

## Gates (run in order inside `commit()`)

**Gate A — Mechanical & Locked:** source must parse (`ast`), exported defs required by
dependents must keep their signatures, and a `LOCKED` node rejects every mutation. **Lock
re-verification:** a commit whose source is byte-identical to the locked node's canonical state,
whose on-disk bytes still hash to its last attestation, is not a mutation — it runs Gates B/C
against the current upstream and lands with the node still `LOCKED` (how a locked module dirtied
by a dependency change returns to clean). Failure: `MechanicalError`. `verified[]` untouched on rejection.

**Gate B — Omission:** AST symbol fingerprinting. Rejects (1) dropped `preserved_symbols[]`
(`INTRA_NODE_SYMBOL_DROPPED`), (2) >15% AST-statement shrinkage without `allow_deletion=True`
(`INTRA_NODE_MASS_DELETION`) — for Python only when the shrink also loses a **binding** (a def,
class, method, or module- / class-level assigned name) or changes an exported signature: a
**concise refactor** that keeps every binding, stubs no body and keeps every Gate C guard passes.
On an *accepted* export-signature change, downstream dependents
transition to `DIRTY_OMISSION_RISK` (`INTER_NODE_DIRTY` propagation). Failure: `OmissionError`.

**Gate C — Logical, Attestation, Telemetry:** every `invariants[]` expression must hold
(failure: `LogicalError`). Each evaluates with `src` (= `ast.unparse(tree)`: normalized,
comment-free, so whitespace never trips it and an invariant can never satisfy itself), `tree`
(`ast.Module`), `ns` (the staged module exec-loaded into an isolated namespace, project imports
resolved to canonical sources — loaded only when referenced), plus `ast` and
`raises(fn, "Exc")`. Sugar: `call:<expr> raises <Exc>`. **Auto-mined invariants:** at analysis time every top-level
function whose body opens with guard clauses (`if <cond on one param>: raise <Exc>`) gets a
synthesized `call:fn(param=value, …) raises Exc` invariant (listed in `invariants_auto_mined`,
de-duplicated against hand-written ones, re-mined on every accepted commit). Mined guards are
waived by `allow_deletion=True`; hand-written invariants never are. When the staged signature
gains required parameters, a mined `call:` invariant is evaluated with typed mocks for them, so
the guard is still exercised (hand-written calls are never filled in). **Structural guard
invariants** (`guard:<Symbol>:<clause>`, Python as well as TS / Go / Rust / Java) need no runtime
arguments, so they cover what `call:` mining cannot — methods (`Class.method`), nested scopes
(`fn.Inner.m`), external types (`isinstance(x, CookieJar)`): every `if <cond> raises <Exc>` at any
depth, every `assert <cond>`, a leading `if <cond> returns <const / None / empty>`, a leading
`if <cond> returns early` when the returned value is computed (the condition is pinned, the
expression may be refactored), every `except <T> raises <Exc>` handler, and `<obj>.get('<key>')
has default` for a `.get('<key>', <literal other than None>)` (any default keeps it; a bare
`<obj>['<key>']` subscript drops it). Clauses are normalized with `ast.unparse` (messages, quotes,
parentheses never matter) and a repeated clause is numbered (`… #2`). Gate C requires each to stay
present anywhere in its symbol's body, after the executable invariants run; a leading guard the
`call:` miner already exercises is left to that semantic check, so an equivalent rewrite passes.
A focused checkout lists only the focus's guards (frontmatter `guard_invariants: N` counts all).
Namespace loading and every evaluation run under an
execution guard (200k line-event steps / 0.5 s backstop); overrun is a deterministic
`LogicalError`. On pass, write the source to the tracked file (UTF-8, keeping the file's BOM and
line endings; a file changed on disk since the kernel last read it is a `MechanicalError` and is
left alone), append a deterministic SHA-256 / DSSE-style envelope whose `sha256` hashes those exact
bytes to `verified[]`, garbage-collect dead-end scratchpad history, and update telemetry.
`omissions_blocked` counts Gate B and Gate C rejections.

Canonical state is always LF. Files that are not valid UTF-8 are left untracked.

## Errors

`GateError` (base) → `MechanicalError` (Gate A), `OmissionError(subtype=...)` (Gate B),
`LogicalError` (Gate C). Subtypes: `INTRA_NODE_SYMBOL_DROPPED`, `INTRA_NODE_MASS_DELETION`,
`INTER_NODE_DIRTY`, `LOCKED_MUTATION`.

## Telemetry terms

Telemetry counts the read path only: a **turn** is a checkout. Commits (patches, whole-source
writes, `sync` adoptions, in-kernel re-verification) charge nothing and add no turn.
**raw_bloated_tokens** — tokens an unfirewalled agent would have paid: full re-read of every
file read so far on each turn, *plus the 5-minute cache-cliff penalty* (a re-read later than 300s
after the previous one is billed again at full input rate, not cache-hit rate).
**compacted_okf_tokens** — tokens actually returned to the agent: CheckoutPayload sizes.
**dollar savings** — `(raw − compacted) / 1e6 × $3.00` (Sonnet-class input rate; constant lives
in one place: `kernel/_telemetry.py`). Token counting is deterministic: `ceil(len(text)/4)`.

## The two public seams (pre-agreed; all tests live here)

**Seam 1 — StateKernel public Python API** (`backend/kernel/__init__.py`):
`init_session(project_root) -> session_id` · `checkout(session_id, node_id, *, focus=None) -> CheckoutPayload`
· `commit(session_id, node_id, source=None, *, patch=None, allow_deletion=False) -> CommitVerdict`
· `lock_node(session_id, node_id)` · `get_telemetry(session_id) -> Telemetry`
· `finalize_session(session_id)` · `record_draft(session_id, node_id, text)` /
`drafts(session_id)` (Door-1 scratchpad support; accepted commits GC that node's drafts).
Catches: compilation, gates, propagation, attestation, telemetry math.
Misses: HTTP serialization — that's Seam 2's job.

**Seam 2 — DualDoorGateway HTTP/MCP boundary** (`backend/server.py`):
`POST /v1/chat/completions` · `POST /v1/messages` · `POST /v1/step/*` ·
`WS /v1/ws/{session_id}` · Streamable HTTP `/mcp`. Door 1 honours `x-stepcheck-focus`
(`"a,b"`, or `""` for a pure skeleton) and folds a ```` ```stepcheck-patch ```` JSON block in the
latest assistant turn as a patch commit.
Catches: proxy pruning/injection, BYOK forwarding + dry-run fallback, MCP tool wiring,
WS state streaming. Misses: kernel internals — already covered at Seam 1.

## Testing rules (skill precedence)

Matt Pocock `tdd` + `codebase-design` override `python-testing-patterns` on mocking:
**never mock internal modules, AST parsers, YAML validators, or hash functions.** Tests hit
Seam 1 / Seam 2 only, against concrete non-tautological fixtures (hand-written literal projects
and hand-calculated expected numbers). `python-testing-patterns` is used only for pytest
fixture parameterization and async test runners.
